item.text: {"chapter_id":"4B","answers":[{"question_id":"4B.1","answer":"The 2023 process combined formal competition with serious implementation defects and disputed contestability. Favorable evidence includes elections held on the constitutional schedule, validation of 26 presidential candidates with two reinstated by the Constitutional Court, broad party registration, municipal elections, diaspora voting, citizen observation, and a CENI-announced mixed external voter-register audit. [BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0001-E015, BATCH-0027-E011, BATCH-0023-E015] Tshisekedi also directed institutions to protect voters and electoral materials and publicly committed to transparency, inclusiveness, equal opportunity, and observation. [BATCH-0009-E001, BATCH-0021-E014] Conversely, observers reported under-registration, delayed voter-list publication and education, accessibility barriers for women, Indigenous people, displaced people, older people, and persons with disabilities, late or closed polling stations, extended voting, procedural deviations, opaque tabulation, conflicting voter totals, duplicated stations, alleged military-school voting, and annulled results. [BATCH-0001-E013, BATCH-0001-E016, BATCH-0002-E023, BATCH-0002-E024, BATCH-0007-E010, BATCH-0005-E002, BATCH-0005-E006, BATCH-0013-E008, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0019-E013, BATCH-0028-E011, BATCH-0028-E014] Voting did not occur in Rutshuru and Masisi because of armed-group control, and women won only 61 of 477 initially confirmed National Assembly seats. [BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E011] The campaign was competitive but included violence, ruling-coalition administrative-resource abuse, attacks involving UDPS supporters, intimidation, and restricted observation. [BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0002-E013, BATCH-0002-E014, BATCH-0002-E018] Tshisekedi was provisionally and later judicially confirmed as winner, while his coalition won a large legislative majority; opposition actors disputed credibility and authorities prohibited a post-election protest. [BATCH-0007-E005, BATCH-0007-E001, BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0021-E009, BATCH-0010-E022] His political coordinator urged acceptance of the results, but this was not a personal acceptance of an adverse result, and no verified opposition victory tested that safeguard. [BATCH-0006-E006] Most operational failures are attributed to CENI, courts, authorities, party supporters, conflict, or logistics rather than personally to Tshisekedi; whether irregularities changed presidential voter intent remains unresolved.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E010","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0001-E015","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0001-E013","BATCH-0001-E016","BATCH-0002-E023","BATCH-0002-E024","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0028-E014","BATCH-0006-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0002-E014","BATCH-0002-E018","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0007-E010","BATCH-0013-E008","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0019-E013","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0028-E011","BATCH-0010-E022"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Personal presidential control over CENI, courts, police, ruling-party supporters, and administrative-resource abuse is not established for most incidents.","The CENI audit was institutionally reported and its completion, independence, and corrective effect are not established.","The effect of irregularities on the presidential result is unresolved.","No verified opposition victory occurred, so acceptance of an adverse transfer was not directly tested.","Conflict-related disenfranchisement and operational failures have multiple causes."]},{"question_id":"4B.2","answer":"The evidence does not show consistent restraint from using state authority in ways that could preserve incumbent or allied power. The clearest ruler-attributed measure was the continued state of siege: Tshisekedi repeatedly extended it, transferred civilian administration in North Kivu and Ituri to military and police officials, replaced elected governors, suspended elected provincial assemblies, and subjected civilians to military courts. [BATCH-0012-R03-E001, BATCH-0012-R03-E002, BATCH-0012-R03-E003, BATCH-0015-E007] Amnesty linked appointed military authorities to harassment, detention, and repression of critics, although personal responsibility for each abuse is not shown. [BATCH-0012-R03-E002] Authorities blocked Katumbi’s travel and opposition sit-ins, used tear gas and beatings, banned demonstrations, arrested opposition figures, and prohibited a post-election march. [BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0021-E009] The Carter Center found ruling-coalition abuse of administrative resources; observers reported electoral irregularities, nontransparent auditing, and perceived CENI proximity to government. [BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0010-E020, BATCH-0013-E009] A governor aligned with Tshisekedi declared him the only candidate in one province, but the evidence does not show presidential authorization or remedy. [BATCH-0006-E004] Tshisekedi nevertheless directed institutions to protect electoral materials, punish fraud and discrimination, and pursue electoral-security procedures; CENI announced an external audit and the Constitutional Court reinstated two candidates. [BATCH-0009-E001, BATCH-0027-E011, BATCH-0005-E005] Support for local armed groups and expanded coercive capacity occurred in wartime, but the record does not establish that these measures were adopted specifically to entrench personal or party power. [BATCH-0028-E016, BATCH-0011-E019] Thus, emergency-rule continuation and government-level electoral restrictions are inconsistent with consistent non-entrenchment, while intent and personal attribution remain uncertain for many local and institutional actions.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E002","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0010-E020","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0009-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0006-E004","BATCH-0028-E016","BATCH-0011-E019"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Personal entrenchment intent is clearest for neither the state-of-siege extensions nor most local restrictions.","Many actions are attributed to CENI, police, provincial authorities, courts, or party supporters rather than directly to Tshisekedi.","The legality, safeguards, and parliamentary role in each emergency extension are incompletely documented.","Conflict provides a material alternative explanation for some coercive measures."]},{"question_id":"4B.3","answer":"Formal protections and limited remedies coexisted with recurring restrictions on opposition, journalists, critics, protest, and civic space. The revised press law guaranteed access to some non-classified public-interest information, and authorities sometimes released detainees, arrested officers after abuses, condemned attacks, or escorted a peaceful protest. [BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0002-E012, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0022-E014] Tshisekedi publicly invoked equality, rejected divisive trends, and said criticism would not deter his security position; these are conduct or rhetoric evidence, not proof of protection in practice. [BATCH-0020-E015, BATCH-0003-E010] Adverse evidence includes the violent May opposition march, blocked opposition meetings, arrests of opposition figures, detention of journalists over reporting or criticism, the Bujakera prosecution, detention and beating of journalists by soldiers, attacks on journalists by ruling-party or allied supporters, and a broadcast shutdown after election-related reporting. [BATCH-0002-E011, BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0003-E005, BATCH-0003-E006, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0026-E007, BATCH-0026-E011, BATCH-0027-E002, BATCH-0027-E003, BATCH-0027-E004, BATCH-0027-E005] The Goma operation against a banned demonstration involved killings, injuries, mass arrests, disputed casualty figures, missing persons, weak investigation, and flawed proceedings against civilians and security personnel. [BATCH-0011-E018, BATCH-0011-E020, BATCH-0011-E021, BATCH-0023-E014] The record also includes intimidation of human-rights defenders and no known investigation of reported sexual and physical violence by UDPS supporters against opposition supporters. [BATCH-0021-E010, BATCH-0021-E011, BATCH-0002-E014] Some corrective steps occurred, but final investigations, accountability, and remedy were generally not established. Most incidents are attributed to state agencies, security forces, regulators, provincial officials, or party supporters rather than a proven personal presidential order; Tshisekedi’s public praise for the police chief after the May operation is a direct adverse signal. [BATCH-0002-E011]","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0011-E021"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E015","BATCH-0003-E010","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0025-E013","BATCH-0027-E005","BATCH-0010-E022","BATCH-0002-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Final outcomes of most investigations and prosecutions are not supplied.","Goma casualty figures and responsibility findings remain disputed or unresolved.","Some violence was committed by opposition or other non-state actors.","The record is limited on NGO registration, satire-specific remedies, and systematic civil-society monitoring.","Personal presidential authorization is not established for most incidents."]},{"question_id":"4B.4","answer":"Courts, election bodies, legislatures, auditors, and rights institutions retained formal or partial checking capacity, but the evidence does not show consistent protection of their independence when they could constrain Tshisekedi. The Constitutional Court validated a broad field of candidates and reinstated two candidates; CENI announced a mixed external register audit; Parliament and the Court of Accounts later scrutinized 2023 budget execution; and the National Commission on Human Rights issued reports, visited detention centers, and followed complaints. [BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0027-E001, BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0024-E003, BATCH-0024-E004, BATCH-0011-E014] Formal safeguards also included judicial appointments, magistrate recruitment, a Court of Auditors procedure framework, and presidentially endorsed ICC cooperation. [BATCH-0015-E006, BATCH-0019-E005, BATCH-0019-E006, BATCH-0016-E010, BATCH-0019-E001] Against this, presidential ordinances revoked, retired, reassigned, promoted, and appointed judges and prosecutors without supplied reasons or selection criteria; the practical effect on tenure and independence is unknown. [BATCH-0015-E006, BATCH-0019-E006] The state of siege replaced elected provincial institutions with military administration and military courts. [BATCH-0012-R03-E003] Observers reported unexplained court decisions, suspected corruption involving electoral judges, perceived politicization of CENI and the Constitutional Court, nontransparent tabulation, and opposition reluctance to litigate because courts were viewed as controlled by power. [BATCH-0001-E016, BATCH-0008-E004, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0028-E017, BATCH-0028-E018, BATCH-0028-E023] Tshisekedi stated he would not intervene in Bujakera’s case, which is a stated separation-of-powers position, but it does not establish fair adjudication or institutional independence. [BATCH-0025-E013] The evidence therefore supports formal institutional capacity and some review, but not reliable protection of jurisdiction, appointments, tenure, funding, local-government autonomy, or decisions that constrained the executive.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0027-E001","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0011-E014","BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E006","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0025-E013"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0001-E016","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0028-E023"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Reasons for judicial removals and appointments, qualifications, tenure protection, and later decisions are not supplied.","Legislative independence, local-government autonomy, and institutional funding are incompletely documented.","Perceived politicization does not itself prove unlawful presidential interference.","The state-of-siege legal text and parliamentary involvement in each extension are not fully shown.","The CENI audit’s independence, completion, and implementation of recommendations are unresolved."]},{"question_id":"4B.5","answer":"The record does not establish politically neutral personnel practice. Tshisekedi made broad judicial appointments and removals, reshuffled the cabinet, appointed public-enterprise and regulatory managers, appointed presidential advisers, and installed new Gécamines leadership; the records provide little information on qualifications, selection criteria, party ties, dismissal reasons, tenure, or performance. [BATCH-0015-E006, BATCH-0019-E005, BATCH-0019-E006, BATCH-0009-E003, BATCH-0008-E014, BATCH-0015-E012, BATCH-0018-E004] ACLED reported concerns that CENI was politically close to government and that Denis Kadima was viewed by critics as close to Tshisekedi. [BATCH-0010-E020] Other reporting described sympathetic judicial appointments and allegations of ethnic or political stacking, but those remain allegations rather than adjudicated findings. [BATCH-0028-E021] Security-sector personnel and aligned armed-group arrangements also raise neutrality and vetting concerns: surrendered fighters were transferred to military training without proper vetting, and government forces supported or operated alongside non-state armed groups. [BATCH-0010-E015, BATCH-0011-E019, BATCH-0028-E016] Formal safeguards existed, including budget-governance controls, audit committees, magistrate recruitment and training, police-investigation capacity, and official instructions emphasizing loyalty to the nation rather than personal interests. [BATCH-0029-E004, BATCH-0029-E005, BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0009-E005, BATCH-0019-E010] These are institutional inputs or rhetoric, not proof of neutral appointments in practice. The evidence does not conclusively establish systematic civil-service loyalty tests, a personality cult, or personal control of every appointment; it does establish substantial risks to neutrality and insufficient evidence that appointments preserved independence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E005","BATCH-0019-E006","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0008-E014","BATCH-0010-E020","BATCH-0028-E021","BATCH-0010-E015","BATCH-0011-E019"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E004","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0009-E005","BATCH-0019-E010","BATCH-0015-E012","BATCH-0018-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Appointment criteria, qualifications, political affiliations, dismissal reasons, and tenure protections are generally unavailable.","There is little direct evidence on ordinary civil-service rules or loyalty tests.","Politicization and ethnic-stacking claims are partly perception-based or allegation-based.","Security-sector personnel decisions occurred amid armed conflict and may reflect operational considerations as well as political loyalty.","Institutional appointment records do not by themselves establish a personality cult."]},{"question_id":"4B.6","answer":"The period shows limited formal openness but a materially pressured information environment. The revised 2023 press law guaranteed access to some non-classified public-interest information and followed consultations, but retained possible prison sentences for press offenses and added a bad-faith false-information restriction; the Digital Code also criminalized dissemination of information deemed false. [BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0011-E011] CENI announced an external register audit with mixed experts and planned publication, and the EU was initially invited to observe nationwide, although the mission was reduced after authorities did not authorize satellite equipment. [BATCH-0027-E011, BATCH-0028-E007, BATCH-0028-E003, BATCH-0002-E018] RSF independently rated the DRC 42.16 and 130th of 180 in its 2023 index, while Tshisekedi claimed a 30-place improvement over four years; the latter is a presidential assertion not independently substantiated by the supplied record. [BATCH-0026-E026, BATCH-0022-E006] Adverse evidence includes a non-independent national broadcaster, political and local-authority pressure, journalist threats, arrests, disappearances, attacks, self-censorship, restricted access to public places and airports, and impunity. [BATCH-0025-E008, BATCH-0025-E025, BATCH-0025-E027, BATCH-0025-E028] Bujakera was detained over a report he did not author, soldiers beat and detained journalists, ruling-party or allied supporters attacked journalists, and CSAC took Perfect Télévision off air after reports on polling problems. [BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0026-E007, BATCH-0027-E002, BATCH-0027-E003, BATCH-0027-E004, BATCH-0027-E005] OLPA reported that provincial media regulation was under-equipped and weak, creating conditions for disinformation and ethnic hate speech. [BATCH-0006-E009] No supplied evidence establishes a nationwide internet shutdown or online-content censorship in 2023, but that absence does not offset the documented legal, administrative, physical, and broadcast pressures. Personal presidential direction of individual abuses is generally unproven; attribution is mainly to state authorities, regulators, security forces, and party supporters.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0028-E003","BATCH-0026-E026","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0006-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E006","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0027-E005","BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0023-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The press-law text’s judicial interpretation and enforcement are not supplied.","The EU mission’s reduction rationale and eventual findings are unresolved.","Media ownership, licensing, and funding transparency are incompletely documented.","The CENI audit’s completion and corrective effect are unknown.","No direct presidential order is shown for most journalist attacks, regulatory actions, or security-force abuses."]},{"question_id":"4B.7","answer":"Formal inclusion measures coexisted with substantial unequal access. Tshisekedi signed the Indigenous Peoples’ rights law, and 2023 laws addressed human-rights defenders, victim reparations, trafficking, and penitentiary principles; these frameworks provided legal assistance, protection, compensation, and guarantees of non-repetition, but implementation and reach were not established. [BATCH-0001-E010, BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0029-E001, BATCH-0029-E002] The electoral process included broad registration, citizen observers, diaspora voting, candidate validation, and reinstatement of two candidates by the Constitutional Court. [BATCH-0001-E015, BATCH-0002-E023, BATCH-0005-E005] Tshisekedi directed institutions to punish exclusion and discrimination in electoral conduct, but enforcement evidence is limited. [BATCH-0009-E001] Adverse evidence includes under-registration, inadequate voter education, inaccessible polling infrastructure, delayed or absent voting, and barriers affecting women, Indigenous people, internally displaced people, older people, and persons with disabilities. [BATCH-0001-E013, BATCH-0002-E023, BATCH-0002-E024] Voting did not occur in conflict-held territories, disenfranchising hundreds of thousands, and women won only 61 of 477 initially confirmed National Assembly seats. [BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E011] Opposition access was restricted when police blocked Katumbi’s travel and opposition sit-ins, used tear gas and beatings, banned demonstrations, and arrested opposition candidates; authorities were also not known to have investigated reported UDPS-linked sexual and physical attacks on opposition supporters. [BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0002-E014] A provincial governor declared Tshisekedi the only candidate in one province, and CSAC condemned the statement as exclusionary and discriminatory, without evidence of presidential endorsement or remedy. [BATCH-0006-E004, BATCH-0002-E017] Tshisekedi publicly promoted equality and opposed division, but rhetoric and formal law do not establish equal political access in practice. Structural gender, disability, conflict, and education disparities are partly inherited or conflict-driven, so personal causation is limited.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E010","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0029-E001","BATCH-0029-E002","BATCH-0001-E015","BATCH-0002-E023","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0001-E013","BATCH-0002-E024","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0028-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E015","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0002-E014","BATCH-0006-E004","BATCH-0002-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Implementation, funding, enforcement, and geographic reach of inclusion laws are not established.","Many adverse outcomes are attributed to CENI, police, provincial officials, party supporters, armed groups, or conflict conditions rather than directly to Tshisekedi.","Complete disaggregated participation data are unavailable.","The president’s authorization, endorsement, investigation, or remedy regarding aligned officials’ exclusionary conduct is not shown.","Formal candidate validation does not establish equal campaign conditions or effective access."]},{"question_id":"4B.8","answer":"Tshisekedi pursued a second five-year term after his party designated him as candidate, and he stated that the Constitution permitted the bid. [BATCH-0005-E008, BATCH-0018-E006] Elections occurred on the normal legal schedule, and the Constitutional Court validated the presidential field and later confirmed the result; these establish formal continuity, not independent succession safeguards. [BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0007-E001] The process was qualified by delayed and extended voting, nonvoting in conflict-affected territories, annulled results, disputed tabulation, irregularities, and allegations that CENI and the Court were politicized. [BATCH-0028-E011, BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0005-E006, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0028-E018] The Constitutional Court’s final confirmation and swearing-in authorization occurred in January 2024, so they are retrospective adjudication of the 2023 election rather than 2023-period events. [BATCH-0007-E001, BATCH-0018-E009] Tshisekedi’s political coordinator urged rival camps to accept the result and prepare for 2028, but this was not a personal response to an adverse result. [BATCH-0006-E006] No opposition victory occurred, so acceptance of a lawful transfer to an opponent was not tested. Normal parliamentary scheduling and legislative elections do not by themselves establish compliance with presidential succession constraints, and the supplied constitutional text is absent. The evidence therefore supports formal continuation and an asserted constitutional second-term basis, but not robust proof that transfer institutions were independent, fully credible, or capable of constraining incumbent continuation.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0028-E010","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0006-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E011","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0007-E001","BATCH-0018-E009","BATCH-0028-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The applicable constitutional term-limit text is not supplied.","The Court’s confirmation is not an independent election-integrity assessment.","No adverse opposition transfer occurred, leaving acceptance untested.","Many irregularities are attributed to CENI, courts, authorities, conflict, or logistics rather than personally to Tshisekedi.","January 2024 adjudication and swearing-in cannot silently expand the target period."]},{"question_id":"4B.9","answer":"The supplied evidence does not establish spyware procurement, targeted interception, surveillance-data use, or a nationwide internet shutdown. The 2023 human-rights assessment instead reported that authorities did not restrict or disrupt internet access or censor online content. [BATCH-0011-E011] Nevertheless, political suppression used legal, administrative, broadcast, and physical mechanisms: the Digital Code criminalized false information; the press law retained prison exposure and added a bad-faith clause; journalists were detained over reporting, criticism, tweets, or alleged false information; and one journalist’s phone was retained for intended examination. [BATCH-0011-E011, BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0026-E011, BATCH-0025-E012] The state of siege, repeatedly extended under Tshisekedi, transferred civilian authority to military and police officials and was linked to harassment, detention, and mass pretrial detention of critics, journalists, activists, and political figures. [BATCH-0012-R03-E001, BATCH-0012-R03-E002, BATCH-0012-R03-E003] CSAC ordered Perfect Télévision off air after reports about polling irregularities, while party-linked supporters attacked journalists. [BATCH-0027-E002, BATCH-0027-E003] The Goma operation against a banned protest involved a planned security operation, killings, arrests, missing persons, disputed casualties, and weak accountability; direct operational responsibility is attributed to regional security authorities rather than proven personally to Tshisekedi. [BATCH-0011-E018, BATCH-0011-E020, BATCH-0011-E021] Tshisekedi convened a state-of-siege review and said he would not intervene in Bujakera’s case, but neither demonstrates effective independent oversight or remedy. [BATCH-0021-E012, BATCH-0025-E013] The result is a documented pattern of legal and administrative suppression, with the specific surveillance and digital-control mechanisms posed by the question largely unproven.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E002","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E020"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0021-E012","BATCH-0025-E013","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0011-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No evidence establishes spyware procurement, targeted interception, surveillance-data access, or a nationwide shutdown.","Absence of reported internet restriction does not establish general digital freedom.","Most incidents are attributed to agencies, regulators, security forces, or party supporters rather than directly to Tshisekedi.","Investigations and remedies were generally incomplete or unverified.","Some casualty and responsibility accounts remain disputed."]},{"question_id":"4B.10","answer":"The evidence does not establish that Tshisekedi left political freedom and democratic resilience durably stronger than inherited by the end of 2023. Favorable formal or capacity-building evidence includes enacted rights and justice laws, recruitment and training of magistrates, selected justice outputs, a CENI external-audit process, a National Commission on Human Rights that monitored detention and complaints, presidential instructions against electoral exclusion and fraud, and some permitted observation and peaceful protest. [BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0011-E014, BATCH-0009-E001, BATCH-0022-E014, BATCH-0019-E001] These measures show institutional activity and stated commitments, but many were externally supported, self-reported, selected, or lacking evidence of independent review, nationwide implementation, correction, or durability. The adverse trajectory is stronger on core democratic-resilience mechanisms: the state of siege replaced elected civilian institutions with military administration and restricted civic space; the 2023 election combined formal competition with serious logistical, transparency, accessibility, observation, violence, and politicization concerns; civic and media space remained pressured by arrests, attacks, protest repression, and broadcaster or legal controls; and transitional justice and accountability remained incomplete. [BATCH-0012-R03-E003, BATCH-0012-R03-E004, BATCH-0012-R03-E007, BATCH-0001-E012, BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0013-E010, BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E014, BATCH-0025-E008, BATCH-0028-E015, BATCH-0010-E016, BATCH-0028-E017, BATCH-0028-E018] UNJHRO recorded a 12% decline in documented violations, but this measures reported incidents rather than democratic resilience and may reflect conflict and reporting conditions. [BATCH-0025-E009] Formal judicial reorganization and election procedures therefore coexist with uncertain independence and implementation. Many adverse outcomes involve collective state institutions, security forces, political parties, armed groups, or conflict conditions rather than proven personal presidential orders; however, Tshisekedi is directly attributable for the state-of-siege framework, repeated extensions, key appointments, public security rhetoric, and formal commitments whose remedies were incomplete. Durability beyond 2023 and a counterfactual against inherited conditions are not demonstrated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0011-E014","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0001-E012","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0025-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R03-E004","BATCH-0012-R03-E007","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0028-E014","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0028-E015","BATCH-0010-E016","BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0022-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No counterfactual establishes change relative to inherited political freedom.","Formal laws, staffing, audits, and selected justice outputs do not establish independent reviewability or durability.","Many adverse findings are government-level or collective and do not prove personal presidential direction.","The CENI audit and government submissions are institutionally interested or self-reported.","The decline in documented violations may reflect reporting or conflict conditions.","Evidence on long-term correction, peaceful transfer, and durable institutional effects is weak."]}],"cross_lens_observations":["Across the ten lenses, formal laws, elections, audits, monitoring, and institutional procedures coexisted with substantial de facto restrictions, emergency-rule centralization, contested electoral administration, civic-space repression, and weak accountability.","Attribution is strongest for Tshisekedi’s state-of-siege decisions, presidential appointments, public directives, candidacy, and stated commitments; it is weaker for operational failures, party-linked violence, CENI conduct, court decisions, and armed-group abuses.","The evidence repeatedly distinguishes stated intent and formal implementation from actual outcomes, independent reviewability, correction, and durability.","Conflict and armed-group control are major constraints, but they do not explain away ruler-attributed institutional substitutions or failures to remedy abuses."]}
